provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

provisions.title: Warning or costs for false or frivolous complaint
provisions.text: (12) At any stage after receipt of a complaint, if the Board is of the opinion that the complaint is false or frivolous, it may issue a warning or impose costs on the complainant.

provisions.title: Body corporate status of Board
provisions.text: (2) The Board shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid, having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power, subject to the provisions of this Act, to acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract and shall, by the said name, sue or be sued.

provisions.title: Procedure to be followed by Board
provisions.text: (1) The Board shall function as an independent body and shall, as far as practicable, function as a digital office, with the receipt of complaints and the allocation, hearing and pronouncement of decisions in respect of the same being digital by design, and adopt such techno-legal measures as may be prescribed.

value.reason: The route GET /api/Complaints is protected only by security.isAuthorized(), which checks that the caller is logged in but not who they are. The handler is the auto-generated finale.resource list endpoint (endpoints `/api/${name}s` and `/api/${name}s/:id`, pagination: false). No ownership filter appears anywhere, such as scoping results to the caller's UserId. As a result, any logged-in user can read every user's complaint records. Those records include UserId, a free-text message (up to 4096 characters) and an uploaded file reference, which is personal data tied to identifiable users. The supplied Evidence shows no object-level or owner-level authorization check, so this fits the rule for an unscoped authenticated read. The /api/Users registration code in the Evidence does not affect this finding. The DPDP Act Section 18 and Section 28 provisions are about the Data Protection Board's own complaint process, not this access-control failure, so they are not cited.
